question: What will be the volume (V) of the cuboid, if its length is doubled, height is halved and breadth is tripled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial volume of the cuboid be V.

Volume depends directly on length, breadth, and height.

Net scaling factor = (Length factor) × (Breadth factor) × (Height factor)

Net factor = 2 × 3 × (1/2) = 3

New Volume = 3 × V = 3V

**∴ The correct answer is 3V.**
